answer: Resist Sybils with gale-tested yarrow bonds. Every agent must plant a yarrow seed bonded to a pearl: a small stake plus a public promise of one verifiable deed, so identity costs real work instead of a fresh key. When the gale blows, a random storm audit each epoch, weak roots are exposed: auditors replay the deed, check its witnesses, and uproot any cluster of identical promises. Honest agents grow deeper roots over time, while copycats must replant after every storm, paying again and again. Old bonds fade unless renewed by new deeds, so standing still means withering.
